description: Club de Ciencias del Colegio San Ignacio
summary: Our project intends to upgrade an already existing device such as Archer, by making it able to recollect even more precise information in faster ways. The new device would be placed in the forearm instead of the wrist, due to the fluid shift, which can interfere with the data recollection and end up giving inaccurate information. Along with this, we made a prototype of a program in which the user will have a journal, a calendar, how much water the crew member is consuming, sleep and mood tracker. In addition, there will also be meditations available, and also entertaining tasks which promote cognitive functions in the crew members.
details:
Our project has two parts, the first one involves wearable technology, based on the already existing ARCHeR. We decided to upgrade the device by adding a faster mechanism of data recollection and changing the placement to the forearm instead of the wrist. This will help to avoid the issues caused by the fluid shift which occurs to astronauts and can sometimes cause problems with the data recollection. We called it H-arm (Health arm).

We used Gemini(SI) in order to create an image of the potential look of the H-arm, as we did not have the resources to actually create any functioning physical prototype of it; we believe that the investments will be worth it if in the long run we wish to do even longer trips. The second part of our project (HEMOSY: HEALTH MONITORY SYSTEM) could be connected to the H-arm, but since we don’t have the functional prototype of the H-arm we were not able to do it, yet.

In space, astronauts are trained to deal with any medical emergency on board; having a system which collects important information and saves it would lower the workload for the crew members.

The second part of the project is a program we made with the tool “Claude” (SI). After our designer made the original design and the different functions available to the user, we had the prototype of the program made.

The program has various diverse equipment to register any bodily changes and possible risk indicators. The program has a daily survey which has questionnaires about not only physical health but also mental health, since one of the main worries about isolation and confinement especially in longer missions is the decline of the crew's mental health and there is not much help available besides the prior training. There will be questions about interpersonal relationships, symptoms for possible health issues, a calendar in case there is an important date that needs to be recorded or the crew might need to be reminded about (as it is not uncommon for astronauts to lose track of the time). There will also be plenty of activities which promote cognitive activity and can be a relieving break from heavy work. These activities were specifically chosen in order to keep the astronauts entertained and maintain an active brain even when not working, without forcing themselves to dedicate their free time to something they don’t find enjoyable. It will also include a mascot which will remind the users to keep a streak to encourage the crew members to complete the daily survey. The design color palette was chosen specifically because of the space theme but also to make it easy to understand even when exhausted. 

The most important aspect is the focus on the crew’s mental health and giving them a chance to have something to remind them of the importance of taking care of themselves both physically and emotionally. Our research found that isolation and confinement can not only cause distress, insomnia/hypersomnia, depressive episodes, change in ideals(and priorities), trouble mantaining interpersonal relationships, and more; all of this can be fatal if not taken care of.

Taking care of the astronauts health will allow them to eventually do longer missions without extreme drawbacks, making it more likely to have better scientific findings important for the entire human species. 

In order to choose the different symptoms we read multiple NASA articles and web pages about the human body in space, and possible worries, issues and troubles that could come up during longer travels through space. We specifically read about the impact of being away for long periods of time in a confined space with little company; the program also registers a journal to help with ventilating frustrations and any negative thoughts that might interfere with communication between crew-mates.
